title: Geometer: Graph Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning via Prototype Representation

problem.claim: Graph few-shot class-incremental learning must classify nodes as graphs evolve and novel classes appear with few labels.

gap.claim: Existing graph neural network methods mainly classify unlabeled nodes in fixed classes with abundant labeling.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes Geometer for graph few-shot class-incremental learning.
Geometer predicts node labels by finding the nearest class prototype instead of replacing and retraining a fully connected classifier.
Geometer adjusts attention-based prototypes using geometric proximity, uniformity, and separability, and introduces teacher-student knowledge distillation and biased sampling.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe Geometer as a novel method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four public datasets are reported to show that Geometer improves over state-of-the-art methods by 9.46% to 27.60%.

narrative_sequence.summary: Node classification is important for real-world graph applications.
Existing graph neural network methods primarily assume fixed classes and abundant labeling, while practical graphs evolve and introduce novel classes with few labels.
The paper proposes Geometer, which uses nearest class prototypes, adjusts attention-based prototypes geometrically, and adds distillation and biased sampling.
The authors report improvements of 9.46% to 27.60% over state-of-the-art methods on four public datasets.

source_observation.claim: The method represents classes with prototypes and predicts labels through nearest-prototype matching.

interpretation.claim: Prototype-based classification can avoid replacing and retraining a fully connected classifier when classes are added incrementally.

application.claim: Consider prototype representations for systems that must accommodate newly emerging classes with limited labels.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when nearest-prototype matching is preferable to classifier retraining beyond the described setting.

unknowns: The four public datasets are not identified.
The evaluation protocol and baseline methods are not described.
The abstract does not provide component-level ablations or implementation details.
